hook: The first verse of the Gita
meaning: Dhritarashtra asked: O Sanjaya, gathered on the holy field of Kurukshetra, eager to fight, what did my sons and the sons of Pandu do?
speaker: Dhritarashtra said

hook: The most famous verse of the Gita
Act, but not for the fruit
meaning: Your right is to action alone, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit be your motive, and do not cling to inaction either.
speaker: Krishna said

meaning: Better is your own duty, even done imperfectly, than another's duty done well. Better to die in your own duty; another's duty is full of fear.
speaker: Krishna said

padas: यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत
meaning: O Bharata, whenever righteousness declines and unrighteousness rises, then I manifest Myself.
speaker: Krishna said

padas: शुनि चैव श्वपाके च पण्डिताः समदर्शिनः
meaning: The wise see with an equal eye a learned and humble Brahmin, a cow, an elephant, a dog and an outcaste.
speaker: Krishna said

meaning: Lift yourself up by your own self; never let yourself sink. For the self alone is your friend, and the self alone is your enemy.
speaker: Krishna said

meaning: At the end of many births, the wise one surrenders to Me, knowing "Vasudeva is all that is". Such a great soul is very rare.
speaker: Krishna said

meaning: Therefore remember Me at all times, and fight. With mind and intellect offered to Me, you will surely come to Me.
speaker: Krishna said

padas: पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति
meaning: Whoever offers Me with love a leaf, a flower, a fruit or a little water, that loving gift of a pure heart I accept.
speaker: Krishna said

padas: अहमादिश्च मध्यं च भूतानामन्त एव च
meaning: O Arjuna, I am the Self seated in the hearts of all beings. I am their beginning, their middle and their end.
speaker: Krishna said

padas: ऋतेऽपि त्वां न भविष्यन्ति सर्वे येऽवस्थिताः प्रत्यनीकेषु योधाः
meaning: I am Time, the mighty destroyer of worlds, come here to consume all people. Even without you, none of the warriors arrayed against you will survive.
speaker: Krishna said

padas: अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च
meaning: One who hates no being, who is friendly and compassionate, free of "mine" and of ego, equal in pleasure and pain, and forgiving: (that devotee is dear to Me.)
speaker: Krishna said

padas: क्षेत्रज्ञं चापि मां विद्धि सर्वक्षेत्रेषु भारत
meaning: O Bharata, know Me as the knower of the field in all fields, all bodies. The knowledge of the field and its knower is, in My view, true knowledge.
speaker: Krishna said

meaning: Sattva, rajas and tamas, the three qualities born of nature, O mighty-armed, bind the imperishable soul to the body.
speaker: Krishna said

meaning: In this world of living beings, the eternal soul is a part of Me. It draws to itself the mind and the five senses that rest in nature.
speaker: Krishna said

meaning: Desire, anger and greed: these three are the gates of hell that destroy the self. Therefore, give up all three.
speaker: Krishna said

padas: देशे काले च पात्रे च तद्दानं सात्त्विकं स्मृतम्
meaning: A gift given because giving is right, to one who cannot repay, at the proper place and time and to a worthy person: that gift is called sattvic.
speaker: Krishna said

padas: अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः
hook: The final word of the Gita
meaning: Abandon all duties and take refuge in Me alone. I will free you from all sins; do not grieve.
speaker: Krishna said
